title: Claim: Home Ministry Agniveer portal data offered for sale, Mathrubhumi reports; no official confirmation
date_note: Mathrubhumi English published it on 21 November (Malayalam edition 22 November); it says the listing came to light in September during Delhi Police dark web surveillance and gives no arrest date or earlier disclosure day.
place: India (country as stated; location of the portal not given)
geo_basis: country level; Delhi Police named as the investigator, no victim site location stated
summary: Mathrubhumi, citing unnamed official sources, reports Delhi Police apprehended a 14-year-old for allegedly hacking an MHA ex-Agniveer career portal and offering over 2,500 personnel records and admin credentials for $500 in cryptocurrency. It says Delhi Police sent a report to the Home Ministry; its Malayalam edition says there has been no official confirmation. A case was registered under the IT Act.
plain: An Indian newspaper reports police caught a teenager who allegedly advertised Agniveer recruits' personal details for sale. The Home Ministry has not confirmed it, and it is unclear whether the data is genuine.
exec: Unconfirmed report of defence-recruit personal data offered for sale; the Home Ministry has not confirmed it.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Mathrubhumi says Delhi Police reported the case to the Home Ministry.
impact: Reported personal records of over 2,500 Agniveer personnel; authenticity not confirmed.

validation.note: One publisher, Mathrubhumi (English 21 Nov, Malayalam 22 Nov), both on unnamed police or official sources; the Malayalam page says there is no official confirmation. No Delhi Police or MHA statement read.
